coverage_note: North Carolina prohibits collective bargaining contracts between any State or local government unit and a labor organization acting as bargaining agent for public employees, and prohibits public-employee strikes; violations of that article are Class 1 misdemeanors. Public employees may still join organizations; this row records the statutory prohibitions.
quote_normalization: quote_binding exact-substring is checked after Unicode NFC and collapsing every run of whitespace (including no-break space) to one space, in both the quote and the text extracted from the captured bytes (HTML: BeautifulSoup get_text; PDF: pdftotext)

governing_statute.value: Prohibition, not a bargaining statute: N.C. Gen. Stat. 95-98 voids any contract between a State or local government unit and a labor organization as bargaining agent for public employees
governing_statute.quote: and any labor union, trade union, or labor organization, as bargaining agent for any public employees of such city, town, county or other municipality, or agency or instrumentality of government, is hereby declared to be against the public policy of the State, illegal, unlawful, void and of no effect.

source.publisher: North Carolina General Assembly, General Statutes of North Carolina
source.title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 95-98

labor_board.null_reason: No North Carolina statute captured creates a public-sector labor relations board; public-sector bargaining contracts are void under 95-98.

ulp_limitation_period.null_reason: No public-sector unfair labor practice procedure exists in the North Carolina statutes captured.

who_may_bargain.value: No public employees may bargain through a labor organization by contract: the prohibition covers cities, towns, counties, other municipalities and State agencies and institutions
who_may_bargain.quote: Any agreement, or contract, between the governing authority of any city, town, county, or other municipality, or between any agency, unit, or instrumentality thereof, or between any agency, instrumentality, or institution of the State of North Carolina, and any labor union, trade union, or labor organization, as bargaining agent for any public employees

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. The right-to-work statute bars requiring dues or fees as a condition of employment, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: No employer shall require any person, as a condition of employment or continuation of employment, to pay any dues, fees, or other charges of any kind to any labor union or labor organization.

source.publisher: North Carolina General Assembly, General Statutes of North Carolina
source.title: N.C. Gen. Stat. 95-82
